patterns.stable_core: Only one day was captured, so this core comes from one day and may not be stable yet. The answer opens with a verdict: Jotform is the best overall form builder because of its advanced features, workflows and design customization. It then splits the choice by use case. Jotform is best overall and has the most features: a large template library, payment collection, conditional logic and workflows. Typeform is best for interactive, conversational forms that show one question at a time. forms.app has the best free plan, with unlimited responses, team seats and AI form generation. Tally has a clean, Notion-style block editor and unlimited free forms and submissions. Google Forms is completely free and simple, good for quick quizzes and feedback. Microsoft Forms is built into Microsoft 365 for basic surveys and quizzes. The answer ends by saying the right pick depends on budget (free or paid), the purpose of the form (payments, surveys, lead generation) and the integrations needed (Notion, Salesforce, Google Sheets).

summary_md:
## What Google keeps saying
We only have 1 day of data so far (9 October 2026), and Google showed an AI answer on that day. So we can't yet say what Google says over and over. These findings are a starting point, not a pattern.

On that day, the answer was about 184 words long. It opened with a clear verdict: **Jotform is the best overall form builder** because of its features, workflows and design options. It then gave six picks by use case:
- Jotform: best overall
- Typeform: best for conversational, one-question-at-a-time forms
- forms.app: best free plan (unlimited responses and team seats)
- Tally: Notion-style editor, unlimited free forms
- Google Forms: free and simple
- Microsoft Forms: for Microsoft 365 users

It ended by asking about budget, the form's purpose and integrations (Notion, Salesforce, Google Sheets). It also embedded a YouTube comparison video.

## Who Google keeps citing
Google cited 9 sources, each once. They were G2, Venture Harbour, Reddit (r/nocode), topformbuilders.com, typeform.com, freeformbuilders.com and three YouTube videos. Brand sites for Jotform, forms.app and Tally were linked by name in the answer. No website was given to check, so we can't say whether yours was cited.

I could read 4 of the 8 pages we checked: G2, Venture Harbour, Typeform and freeformbuilders.com. Reddit and YouTube were blocked. topformbuilders.com returned no readable text.

## What the winning pages do
- **freeformbuilders.com** does the most useful work. A ranking table comes right after the headline. It lists response limits, prices and screenshots of each tool's pricing page, and explains how it tested. Google used it for 4 of its 6 picks.
- **G2** gives review scores: Jotform 4.7 from 5,324 reviews, Tally 4.9 from 159. It has no prices and no clear winner.
- **Venture Harbour** covers 25 tools and has a price table. But it skips Tally, forms.app and Microsoft Forms, and its answer only comes near the end.
- **Typeform's page** is a sales page with its own claims, such as "95% of the Fortune 500".

The gaps are clear. No page states "Jotform is best overall" and explains why, even though Google opens with that. The sources disagree on numbers: Typeform's starting price is $35 on one page and about $29 on another, and Jotform's template count is 10,000+ in one place and 20,000+ in another. And no page compares the integrations Google asks about.

## What your page needs
- Open with a one-paragraph answer that names Jotform as best overall and lists the five other picks by use case.
- Follow with one table: each tool, what it's best for, free-plan limits, starting price and the date you checked.
- Give each of the six tools its own short section, in Google's order.
- Add a table showing which tools work with Notion, Salesforce and Google Sheets.
- Explain how you tested, and end with an FAQ.
- Keep tracking this search for at least 6 more days to confirm what stays stable.

**The single most important thing:** publish a table of free-plan limits and prices for these six tools that you have checked yourself and clearly dated. Today's sources disagree, and Google needs one it can trust.
